text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Merita Bank opens several representative offices in the Finnish countryside in May.
- State does not have to stump up pay for foreigners working illegally in Finland, Supreme Administrative Court ruled.
- Controversial plan to extend restrictions on sale or transfer of apartments built under state-subsidied housing system ARAVA due in parliament today. @
- Strike in public transport in Helsinki area averted by last-minute agreement.
- New financial newspaper to be published by Sanomat will be called Taloussanomat.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Votes in Nokia increasingly concentrated in the hands of UPM-Kymmene, with 10.4 percent of the votes, and Pohjola, with 5.0 percent, as of May 6. @

- Finnair marketing chief Leif Lundstrom says cooperation with Lufthansa is important, but not as important as sometimes is said. Says Finnair not afraid of Lufthansa's intensifying cooperation with SAS.
- Alliances are Orion's strategy for internationalisation.
- Enskilda Securities aims to be strong in arranging Finnish share offerings and mergers and acquisitions, says corporate finance head. @
AAMULEHTI
- Use of nuclear power not ruled out as an energy source, goverment decided on Wednesday, but future energy strategy will concentrate on boosting the use of natural gas and wood.
- The Ministry of Social Affairs and Health is planning to abolish the Social Insurance Institution's (KELA) compensation payments for private doctor visits, private doctors say.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Bank of Finland sees no need to raise key interest rates, says Matti Vanhala, member of the central bank board of management. @
- U.S. theme park company featuring the Moomins -- the comic characters created by Tove Jansson, will seek Nasdaq listing.
DEMARI
- No return to a floating markka, the government decided finishing up its report to parliament on EMU.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
